text:
Definitions and notation

Let omega be the angular frequency, in rad/min.
Let i be the imaginary unit.
The dead time is theta = 1.5 min.
The process, valve and sensor together, without the controller, are

    G_v(i omega) G_p(i omega) G_m(i omega)
      = 2.0 exp(-1.5 i omega) /
        [(1 + 6 i omega)(1 + 2 i omega)(1 + i omega)(1 + 0.5 i omega)]

since G_v = 1.

For a first-order factor 1 + i omega T, with T the time constant in min,
the magnitude contribution is 1 / sqrt(1 + (omega T)^2) and the phase
contribution is -arctan(omega T).

Hence, with the phase in radians and continuous (unwrapped),

    phase of G_v G_p G_m
      = -1.5 omega - arctan(6 omega) - arctan(2 omega)
        - arctan(omega) - arctan(0.5 omega)              (1)

and

    |G_v G_p G_m|
      = 2.0 / [ sqrt(1 + 36 omega^2) sqrt(1 + 4 omega^2)
                sqrt(1 + omega^2) sqrt(1 + 0.25 omega^2) ]   (2)

(a) Ultimate frequency

The ultimate frequency omega_u is the lowest omega > 0 at which the
phase in (1) equals -180 degrees, i.e. -pi rad:

    1.5 omega_u + arctan(6 omega_u) + arctan(2 omega_u)
      + arctan(omega_u) + arctan(0.5 omega_u) = pi        (3)

Evaluating the left-hand side of (3):

    omega = 0.40 rad/min:  sum = 173.5 degrees
    omega = 0.42 rad/min:  sum = 179.1 degrees
    omega = 0.423 rad/min: sum = 180.0 degrees
        (dead time 36.4 degrees; arctan terms 68.5, 40.2, 22.9
         and 12.0 degrees, totalling 143.6 degrees)
    omega = 0.43 rad/min:  sum = 181.9 degrees

The left-hand side is monotonically increasing in omega, so the
lowest (and here relevant) root is

    omega_u = 0.423 rad/min.

(b) Ultimate gain and ultimate period

At omega_u the loop with a proportional controller K_c is at the
stability limit when K_c |G_v G_p G_m(i omega_u)| = 1, so the
ultimate gain K_u is 1 / |G_v G_p G_m(i omega_u)|.

From (2) at omega_u = 0.423 rad/min, omega_u^2 = 0.179 min^-2 in the
squared-frequency sense, and

    sqrt(1 + 36 omega_u^2) = 2.73
    sqrt(1 + 4 omega_u^2)   = 1.31
    sqrt(1 + omega_u^2)     = 1.086
    sqrt(1 + 0.25 omega_u^2) = 1.022

    product = 2.73 x 1.31 x 1.086 x 1.022 = 3.97
    |G_v G_p G_m(i omega_u)| = 2.0 / 3.97 = 0.504
    K_u = 1 / 0.504 = 1.98 (dimensionless)

The ultimate period is

    P_u = 2 pi / omega_u = 2 pi / 0.423 = 14.8 min.

(c) Ziegler-Nichols PID settings

    K_c   = 0.6 K_u = 0.6 x 1.98 = 1.19 (dimensionless)
    tau_I = P_u / 2 = 14.8 / 2 = 7.42 min
    tau_D = P_u / 8 = 14.8 / 8 = 1.86 min

with tau_I the integral time and tau_D the derivative time, in min.

For the remainder, the controller is

    G_c(s) = 1.19 (1 + 1 / (7.42 s) + 1.86 s)

so at s = i omega,

    G_c(i omega) = 1.19 [ 1 + i (1.86 omega - 1 / (7.42 omega)) ]

with controller magnitude factor
sqrt(1 + (1.86 omega - 1/(7.42 omega))^2) and controller phase
arctan(1.86 omega - 1/(7.42 omega)).
The open-loop transfer function is L = G_c G_v G_p G_m, so its phase
is the controller phase plus the phase in (1), and its magnitude is
1.19 times the controller magnitude factor times the magnitude in (2).
At omega -> 0+ the factor 1/(7.42 i omega) dominates, so the phase of
L starts at -90 degrees, as stated.

(d) Gain margin

Tabulating the phase of L from the expressions above:

    omega = 0.50 rad/min: phase of L = -200.2 + 33.4 = -166.8 degrees
    omega = 0.55 rad/min: phase of L = -212.3 + 37.8 = -174.5 degrees
    omega = 0.58 rad/min: phase of L = -219.3 + 40.2 = -179.2 degrees
    omega = 0.585 rad/min: phase of L = -179.9 degrees
    omega = 0.60 rad/min: phase of L = -223.9 + 41.7 = -182.3 degrees

Hence the first (lowest) phase-crossover frequency is

    omega_pc = 0.586 rad/min.

At omega_pc = 0.586 rad/min, from (2), omega_pc^2 = 0.343:

    denominator product
      = sqrt(1 + 36 x 0.343) sqrt(1 + 4 x 0.343)
        sqrt(1 + 0.343) sqrt(1 + 0.25 x 0.343)
      = 3.66 x 1.54 x 1.16 x 1.04 = 6.80
    |G_v G_p G_m| = 2.0 / 6.80 = 0.294

Controller term: 1.86 x 0.586 - 1/(7.42 x 0.586)
                = 1.090 - 0.230 = 0.857,
controller magnitude factor = sqrt(1 + 0.857^2) = 1.32.

    |L(i omega_pc)| = 1.19 x 1.32 x 0.294 = 0.461

The gain margin, as a ratio, is

    GM = 1 / |L(i omega_pc)| = 1 / 0.461 = 2.17.

(e) Phase margin

Tabulating |L|:

    omega = 0.28 rad/min: |L| = 1.01
    omega = 0.284 rad/min: |L| = 1.00
    omega = 0.30 rad/min: |L| = 0.94

so the (unique) gain-crossover frequency is

    omega_gc = 0.284 rad/min.

Phase at omega_gc = 0.284 rad/min, from (1):
dead time 0.426 rad = 24.4 degrees;
arctan terms: arctan(1.704) = 59.6 degrees,
arctan(0.568) = 29.6 degrees, arctan(0.284) = 15.8 degrees,
arctan(0.142) = 8.1 degrees; total process-plus-sensor phase
= -(24.4 + 59.6 + 29.6 + 15.8 + 8.1) = -137.5 degrees.
Controller term: 1.86 x 0.284 - 1/(7.42 x 0.284)
               = 0.527 - 0.474 = 0.053,
controller phase = arctan(0.053) = 3.0 degrees.
Phase of L = -137.5 + 3.0 = -134.5 degrees.

Phase margin = 180 degrees - 134.5 degrees = 45.5 degrees.

(f) Maximum sensitivity

The sensitivity function is S(i omega) = 1 / (1 + L(i omega)).
Writing r = |L(i omega)| and phi = phase of L(i omega),

    |1 + L|^2 = 1 + r^2 + 2 r cos(phi),
    M_s contribution at each omega = 1 / sqrt(1 + r^2 + 2 r cos(phi)).

Evaluating r and phi from the magnitude and phase expressions above:

    omega (rad/min)    r        phi (degrees)   |S|
    0.284              1.00     -134.5          1.29
    0.35               0.81     -144.0          1.70
    0.40               0.70     -151.5          1.96
    0.43               0.65     -156.0          2.06
    0.45               0.62     -159.1          2.10
    0.47               0.59     -162.2          2.12
    0.50               0.55     -166.8          2.09
    0.586              0.46     -180.0          1.86

For omega -> 0, |L| -> infinity through the integral term, so
|S| -> 0; for omega -> infinity, |L| -> 0, so |S| -> 1. The tabulated
interior maximum is therefore the global maximum: the smallest value
of |1 + L| occurs near omega = 0.47 rad/min, where
|1 + L|^2 = 1 + 0.59^2 + 2 x 0.59 x cos(-162.2 degrees)
         = 1 + 0.350 - 1.127 = 0.223,
|1 + L| = 0.472, and |S| = 1 / 0.472 = 2.12.

    M_s = 2.12 at omega = 0.47 rad/min.

Final answers

FINAL (a): 0.423 rad/min
FINAL (b): 1.98 dimensionless, 14.8 min
FINAL (c): 1.19 dimensionless, 7.42 min, 1.86 min
FINAL (d): 2.17 dimensionless, 0.586 rad/min
FINAL (e): 45.5 degrees, 0.284 rad/min
FINAL (f): 2.12 dimensionless, 0.47 rad/min
